name: WARDEN Mobile
subtitle: No account. No telemetry.
promotionalText: A private entry point for people who run networks: no account, no analytics, no sensor access, and a posture screen that states only what is actually enforced.
description:
WARDEN Mobile is a privacy-first browser for security and network administrators, and the mobile companion to WARDEN for Windows.

It is a browser, not a launcher. Pages render in the app's own engine, with WARDEN's address bar, back, forward, reload and a progress line above them — not another app's screen. Requests to known ad and tracker hosts are refused before they leave the app, and the empty slot a blocked ad leaves behind is removed so the page closes up.

WHAT IT DOES
• A real browser surface: the page and its chrome belong to the app, so the address you typed is not handed to a browser you do not control.
• Ad and tracker blocking: ad and tracker hosts are blocked at the request level, and the cosmetic pass removes the containers a blocked ad leaves behind.
• The session is not kept: cookies, web storage and cache are cleared when the browser closes. No history, no profile, no account.
• No third-party cookies: a page keeps its own session cookie so a login still works, and nothing follows the reader between sites.
• Ships no analytics, crash-reporting or advertising SDKs, and requests no camera, microphone or location access.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO YET
• It does not encrypt DNS, and it does not isolate tabs: DNS over HTTPS and per-tab isolation are planned in the public repository, and the app says so on its own screen rather than implying otherwise.
• The desktop build's operator surfaces — shell, mail, messaging and site deconstruction — are not part of the mobile app.
• There is no account, no purchase, no subscription and nothing to configure before the first page loads.

WHO IT IS FOR
Administrators who want a small, auditable browser on a phone that asks for no permissions and phones home to nobody.

PRIVACY
Data collected: none. Full policy: https://innotelinc.github.io/warden/privacy.html

answers.Unrestricted Web Access: Yes — the address field opens any public URL. This is the capability that sets the rating; Chrome, Firefox and DuckDuckGo are all rated 16+ for the same reason.
answers.Violence, Profanity, Horror, Medical, Al: None — the app ships no content of its own beyond its own interface text.
answers.In-App Controls: None claimed. The app has no content of its own to gate.

ageRating.note: App Store Connect now uses 4+/9+/13+/16+/18+, and the questionnaire requires answers for new submissions. Answering 'Unrestricted Web Access' honestly is what produces 16+; do not answer 4+ to make the listing look friendlier.

reviewNotes:
WARDEN Mobile is a browser for security and network administrators, and the mobile companion to an existing desktop product whose source is public at https://github.com/innotelinc/warden. No sign-in, demo account or purchase is required, and no permission prompt appears at any point.

HOW TO TEST
1. Launch the app. The first screen is an address field and a 'Session posture' list that states in plain language what the app does and does not do.
2. Type a host such as example.com and press return, or tap a Quick destination. The page opens in WARDEN's own browser view: an address bar showing the URL, back, forward, reload, and a progress line. It is a WKWebView presented by the app, with WARDEN's chrome around it — not a link out to Safari.
3. Type a news site that carries display advertising and note that the ad requests are refused and their slots removed from the page.
4. Tap Done to return to the app; the session's cookies and cache are discarded at that point. The camera, microphone, location, contacts and tracking permissions are never requested.

WHY THIS IS NOT A WRAPPER AROUND ONE WEBSITE
The app bundles no site, runs no server of its own and has no account, so there is no website being repackaged. It renders pages in a WKWebView the app owns, applies its own content blocking and cosmetic cleanup to them, and supplies its own chrome, address resolution (bare host, IP address or search term) and posture screen.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT
DNS over HTTPS, per-tab isolation and the desktop build's operator surfaces (shell, mail, messaging, site deconstruction) are on the public roadmap and are not in this build. The app says that on its own first screen, and the description says it too, rather than implying protections it does not have.

AGE RATING
'Unrestricted Web Access' is answered Yes, because the address field opens any public URL. That answer is what sets the rating to 16+.

EXPORT COMPLIANCE
ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption is false in Info.plist: the app uses only the HTTPS provided by the operating system and implements no cryptography of its own. App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy declares no tracking and no collected data, and no required-reason API beyond the two Capacitor's bridge touches (UserDefaults and file timestamps).

notes: Push a v* tag: .github/workflows/mobile-ios.yml archives, exports and uploads the build to TestFlight. Manual runs stop at the archive unless upload_to_testflight (publish) or export_signed_ipa (sideload only) is ticked. Check processing with the 'iOS build status' workflow. Fill App Privacy as 'Data Not Collected' — App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy says the same inside the bundle. Answer 'Unrestricted Web Access: Yes' for the 16+ rating.
